text.p: Roland Europe, the Italian based producer of electronic musical instruments, said its net operating profit rose 30 percent to 14.8 billion lire in 1996.
The group said in a statement issued after a board meeting its gross operating margin rose 32 percent to 18.5 billion lire.
The company said it is considering paying out the same dividend of 200 lire a share for 1996 as it did in 1995, and it is also considering a special dividend for 1996.

Group sales for the year slipped 1.5 percent to 107.8 billion lire due to the weakness of the Ecu. In the two years 1995 and 1996, the value of the Ecu fell eight percent while Roland Europe's sales in Ecus rose seven percent.
The company, listed on the Milan stock market since June 1996, is controlled by Roland Corp of Osaka.
